text:
Sophia Rivera: FYI - saw three cold-start incidents in eu-west-1 over past 24h where GPU jobs sat pending 30-90s. Not a huge outage but spikes show up in SLIs. Anyone digging into root cause?

Kenji Nakamura: I'm looking. Early signs point to image-pull + node bootstrap time + aggressive scale-to-zero. When CA triggers new GPU nodes they pull ~10GB of images from our internal registry -- sometimes the registry is the slow link.

Amir Patel: +1. Also noticed kubelet log spam about cgroups and plugin timeouts during init which delays kube-proxy and CNI, so pods wait after node ready.

Leah Ortiz: Are these preemptible nodes? If so boot times and retry jitter can be worse.

Kenji Nakamura: They are preemptible in eu-west to control costs. We have a small on-demand fallback pool but CA often prefers preemptible. CA cooldown settings are low (scale-up instant, scale-down after 2m), so bursts cause scale-up then immediate scale-down of baseline nodes.

Sophia Rivera: Thinking out loud: keep a tiny hot pool of 1-2 GPU nodes per AZ as a baseline to mask cold starts, plus a transient surge pool with longer lifecycle and image pre-warm. Cost vs latency tradeoff. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

Amir Patel: That matches my feeling. Two practical mitigations that together are cheap: 1) image pre-pull DaemonSet on surge nodes; 2) mirror critical images to a registry cache in eu-west. Both cut pull time a lot.

Kenji Nakamura: Agreed. Also we can adjust cluster-autoscaler flags: increase --scale-down-unneeded-time and add --balance-similar-node-groups and a small drain jitter to avoid synchronized drains. Example config snippet I'm testing: 

```
apiVersion: autoscaler/v1
kind: ClusterAutoscaler
spec:
  scaleDown:
    enabled: true
    delayAfterAdd: 10m
    delayAfterDelete: 2m
    delayAfterScale: 5m
  balanceSimilarNodeGroups: true
  scaleDownUnneededTime: 15m
```

Kenji Nakamura: That gives nodes time to accept more requests before being torn down.

Leah Ortiz: Could we also add a label-based hot-pool (nodePool=hot-gpu) with minSize 1 per AZ and use CA's minReplica flag for those groups? That way we don't keep too many on-demand machines but ensure one warm node.

Amir Patel: Yep. And for cost, we can have a small policy: if average GPU usage <5% for 24h, scale hot-pool to 0 overnight in non-prod regions only. Prod keeps min>=1.

InfraBot: [deploy] cluster-autoscaler/eu-west config updated to experimental values by kenji at 1780054405

Sophia Rivera: @Kenji can you test end-to-end: mirror registry > pre-pull DS > CA flags > hot-pool min=1? If we get boot latency down to <10s for pod readiness that's a big win.

Kenji Nakamura: On it. I'll run a synthetic burst test with k6 jobs hitting our infra and capture pod pending->ready histograms. ETA ~3h.

Amir Patel: For the synthetic test, include noisy-network emulation (packet loss, slow registry) so we validate worst-case. Also log the node kubelet and CNI events.

Leah Ortiz: Quick checklist for the playbook (short):
- create node pool hot-gpu (min=1 per AZ) :label nodepool=hot-gpu
- deploy registry mirror in eu-west and update imagePullSecrets
- daemonset pre-pull on surge nodes with tolerations
- adjust CA flags (scaleDown unneeded -> 15m, delayAfterAdd 10m)
- add small random drain jitter (30-120s)
- run synthetic burst + network fault test

Sophia Rivera: Love it. Add a note to runbook about rollback: if cost delta > 15% after 48h, revert hot-pool -> min=0 and revisit image cache.

Kenji Nakamura: Will post results in this thread when tests finish. Initial metric I'll capture: pod_pending_95, pod_ready_p50, image_pull_seconds_p95.

Amir Patel: One more: consider a lightweight warm-bootstrap container that runs at node startup to preconfigure nv_peer_mem and persistence for drivers so first job doesn't need to do that. That cut our 2019 cold-starts a lot.

Sophia Rivera: Good call. Assigning follow-ups: Kenji (test + CA flags), Amir (bootstrap container + pre-pull DS), Leah (hot-pool infra + cost guardrails). I'll create GH issues and link. :thumbsup:

InfraBot: [issue] #4521 created by Sophia Rivera linking this thread at 1780054620

Kenji Nakamura: Test started. I'll drop logs and a short summary when done.

Leah Ortiz: Thanks team. Small wins here will improve customer-facing latency for bursty apps.

Sophia Rivera: Cheers — queueing this for next infra retro.
